$comment: Warden seat permission profile (backported from Proofdelve 21f.1, {{FORT_NAME}}). Loaded by fort/scripts/warden.sh with --setting-sources '' so this file is the ONLY permission source. The launcher also restricts the tool set to Bash,Read,Grep,Glob (no Edit/Write/Task), sets cwd to a scratch copy, and adds the checkout(s) via --add-dir. The seat has ZERO write permissions: the launcher records the verdict (bd comment --file from the session log) and emits the review.verdict event. IMPORTANT, verified 2026-08-03: commands absent from the allow list are NOT reliably denied — Claude Code's built-in classifier auto-allows some read-only commands (sed ran; awk and python failed shut; mutating forms like sed -i and redirection were refused). Treat the allow list as convenience, the deny list as the boundary, and assume unknown read-only commands may run. Hence the broad Bash(*.env*) deny; obfuscated-path reads are a known limit (Proofdelve 21f.8): deny globs bind a spelling, not a file. Deny globs match the whole command line INCLUDING quoted arguments — prose containing a denied pattern trips the rule. NOTE (fortkit-f3y / fortkit-4wlz, 2026-08-11): this list carries NO Read() deny for .ssh, .aws, or absolute-path .env spellings, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. seat-sandbox.sh masks $HOME/.ssh and $HOME/.aws as tmpfs (MASK_DIRS) and binds every .env* over /dev/null at the INODE, so those paths are unreadable by every spelling including ones nobody has thought of. The lines that used to sit here were rendered with a leading double slash (Read(//home/...)), a spelling no real path has, so they bound nothing and inflated an auditor's confidence. Do not re-add absolute-path denies here: the kernel mask is the boundary, and a deny list that looks longer than it is costs more than it buys.
